purpose: Render an ordered collection with optional single or multiple selection while leaving data and row meaning to the consumer.
useWhen: records are read as an ordered collection rather than compared across columns
the same row intent must adapt to Web and native list/detail presentation
avoidWhen: headers and cross-record comparison require a semantic Table
very large interactive data needs an approved virtualization engine
accessibility: Uses ul and li semantics for a simple collection and listbox/option semantics only when selection is enabled.
Selection state, disabled state, keyboard movement, and collection status remain programmatically available.
Consumers must provide an accessible label and stable row keys; row activation and selection are explicit interaction modes.
responsive: Rows reflow within a bounded collection surface without changing item meaning.
The semantic contract can map to native rows, cards, or list/detail without a mobile-only component.
Large collections require a renderer or approved engine adapter to own measurement and windowing.
motion: Uses shared state and interaction transitions.

api.name: items
api.description: Ordered records rendered by the collection.

api.name: rowKey
api.description: Returns the stable opaque identity used for focus and selection.

api.name: renderItem
api.description: Renders consumer-owned row content inside the canonical list semantics.

api.name: interactionMode
api.description: Makes row selection and row activation policy explicit.

api.name: onSelectionChange
api.description: Reports normalized selection without owning business rules.

api.name: error
api.description: Communicates a collection or refresh error.

api.name: hasActiveFilter
api.description: Distinguishes filtered empty from no data.

api.name: loadingMore
api.description: Communicates incremental loading without implying virtualization.

dataCollection.intent: Render a generic ordered collection with optional single or multiple selection without owning domain data.
useWhen: records are read as an ordered collection rather than compared across columns
the same row anatomy must adapt to Web and native list presentation
avoidWhen: cross-record column comparison requires a semantic Table
100,000 interactive rows need an approved virtualization engine
dataCollection.rowCountSuitability: bounded and medium collections; large counts require the normalized virtualization adapter boundary
compatibility: SelectableList is a selection-mode variant of List, not a second primitive.
GroupedList is a composition/recipe concern until a distinct interaction contract is proven.
